time-domain variables according to reducing ECG time duration (*p<0.001) 
Abstract—We investigated the availability of ultra-short term 
ECG for HRV time -domain ana lysis. We obtained 5-minute 
ECG from 28 subjects, then divided it into 300 pieces per every 
reduced time duration: 10, 20, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, 210, 240 
and 270 s. Results showed that the AVNN is stationary in every 
signal duration. However, SDSD and RMSSD, and SDNN, 
NN50 and pNN50 are only stationary in >210 s and >240 s , 
respectively. Statistically, AVNN and SDSD show ed a 
significant coherence in every signal duration. However, other 
variables need minimum signal length to maintain coherence 
with 5-min HRV; > 210 s in SDNN, > 10 s in RMSSD, > 270 s in 
NN50 and >10 s in pNN50. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
Reducing the testing time of heart rate variability (HRV) 
has been consistently needed according to the wide spreading 
of the personal HRV-based applications. Most of research 
related to the ultra-short term HRV has been carried out to find 
the minimum recording time guaranteeing the significant 
result compared with 5-min HRV, then they showed that the 
minimum time requirement is differentiated by the type of 
variable [1, 2]. Those researches might provide the insight for 
the efficient recording duration for HRV analysis. However, 
they did not consider the non-stationarity of bio-signal, thus 
more generalized result which does not depend on the 
recording duration could not be suggested. In this research, we 
investigated the stochastic characteristics followed by 
reducing the signal duration and validated st atistically to 
suggest a minimum time duration of ECG recording for time 
domain analysis of HRV. 
II. MATERIALS AND METHODS 
We obtained ECG from 28 volunteers (8 females, 22±2.9 
years old, 170.2±7.3 cm, 70.5±15.4 kg) in the supine position 
during a rest condition. Every signal was recorded with 
20-minute length, and sampling frequency was 10 kHz. To 
investigate the effect of time -reducing to the HRV analysis, 
we generated the reduced time dataset: 270, 240, 210, 180, 
150, 120, 90, 60, 30, 20 and 10 s-length dataset. Every dataset 
consists of evenly spaced 300 segments within 5 minutes with 
overlapping time . Then, s egments were shuffled randomly. 
Typical time domain variables of HRV, AVNN, SDNN, 
SDSD, RMSSD, NN50 and pNN50, were calculated in each 
reduced time dataset. To test stationarity of variables, we used 
augmented Dickey-Fuller test [3] as an unit root test for a time 
series. Then, one -way ANOVA and Bonferroni’s post- hoc 
test were performed to evaluate the statistical significance of 
the reduced time HRVs compared with 5-minute HRV. 
III. RESULT AND DISCUSSION 
Table I shows that the AVNN is stationary in every ECG 
duration. However, SDSD and RMSSD, and SDNN, NN50 
and pNN50 are only stationary in >210 s and >240 s, 
respectively. Statistically, AVNN and SDSD showed a 
coherence in every ECG duration. How ever, other variables 
showed significant difference( p<0.001) and need minimum 
duration to maintain coherence with 5-minute HRV: > 210 s in 
SDNN, > 10 s in RMSSD, > 270 s in NN50 and >10 s in 
pNN50 (see Fig. 1). 
IV. CONCLUSION 
In this research, we showed that the ultra-short term HRV 
could be a non -stationary according to the analyzing time 
point or variable type. Because stationarity could be changed 
by recording situation, further studies in various conditions are 
needed to generalize the result.
